fields.description:
Mirror inventory finding F9 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), LOW.

## Problem

- `src/rebar/config.py:326` `LAYER_ORDER = ("default", "user", "project", "env", "cli")` — canonical
- `src/rebar/_operation_config.py:51` `_SOURCE_KINDS` — the same 5, hand-copied

`_operation_config.py:128` validates a provenance label against the copy, and `config.py:337`
documents that domain as "``label`` ∈ :data:`LAYER_ORDER`" — so the copy is asserting membership of
the canonical tuple while restating it.

## Approach — a DEFERRED, cached derivation (a module-scope import would cycle)

The obvious fix — `_SOURCE_KINDS = frozenset(config.LAYER_ORDER)` at module scope — does NOT
work, and the reason is the substance of this ticket. The dependency runs the OTHER way:
`config.py:99-101` imports `ENVELOPE_VERSION`, `OperationSnapshot` and `active_snapshot` FROM
`rebar._operation_config`. `_operation_config` is the LEAF (its imports are stdlib only), so a
module-scope `from rebar.config import LAYER_ORDER` would close the loop
config -> _operation_config -> config at import time.

So derive it behind a cached accessor with a deferred import:

    @functools.cache
    def _source_kinds() -> frozenset[str]:
        from rebar.config import LAYER_ORDER
        return frozenset(LAYER_ORDER)

`functools` is already imported here, and the deferred-import pattern is ALREADY established in
this module for exactly this cycle — `:199-200` does `from rebar import config as _config` inside
a function. There is one consumer (`:128`), so the constant-to-accessor change is contained.

ORDER is the tuple's only additional fact, and that consumer uses it purely as a membership test
(`label not in ...`), so a frozenset loses nothing. That is worth stating rather than assuming: a
set derivation would be wrong if any consumer depended on precedence, and none does — the only
other reader of `LAYER_ORDER`, `_commands/show_config.py:52`, takes `list(...)` from config
directly and is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: the source-kind vocabulary is derived from `config.LAYER_ORDER`, not re-listed.
      Verified by a test asserting equality with `frozenset(config.LAYER_ORDER)` and the literal
      being gone.
- [ ] AC1b: the derivation is deferred, so importing `rebar._operation_config` alone does NOT
      import `rebar.config`. Verified by a test that imports the module in a clean interpreter
      and asserts `rebar.config` is absent from `sys.modules` until the accessor is called.
- [ ] AC2: a layer added to `LAYER_ORDER` is accepted as a provenance label with no second edit.
      Verified by a test that extends the compared tuple and asserts the derived set follows.
- [ ] AC3: no consumer of `_SOURCE_KINDS` relies on ordering, so the tuple -> frozenset conversion
      is safe. Verified by a test asserting every use site treats it as a membership set.
- [ ] AC4: an unknown provenance label is still rejected. Verified by an explicit rejection test.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "operation_config or config_layer or provenance" -q` — AC1-AC4.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
